newsitem.title: INDIA: India allows up to 40 pct foreign airline stakes.
newsitem.headline: India allows up to 40 pct foreign airline stakes.

text.p: The Indian cabinet agreed on Friday to allow foreign investors to take equity stakes of up to 40 percent in domestic airlines, Civil Aviation Secretary Yogesh Chandra said.
Chandra told reporters that the Cabinet Committee on Foreign Investment also agreed that any airline controlled by an Indian national would be able to operate freely in India.

Chandra said the cabinet, however, did not decide whether foreign airlines would be allowed to take an equity stake in an Indian operator. Singapore Airlines Ltd and India's Tata group have proposed a $600 million tie-up which Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim has vehemently opposed.
Since India launched economic reforms in 1991, the government has allowed foreign investors, including airlines, to take stakes in domestic airlines on a case-by-case basis.
But Ibrahim's outspoken opposition to the entry of foreign airlines had called into question the possibility of any further foreign investment in the growing sector.

"The decision is to go along with the existing policy which permits 40 percent equity in domestic airlines," Chandra said. He said under the new policy, any airline owned by an Indian national "will have the right of free entry and exit in the Indian skies".
